title: Reviewing Police's Operating Procedures to Minimise Occurrences of Wrongful Arrest
what_it_is: Reviewing Police's Operating Procedures to Minimise Occurrences of Wrongful Arrest

sections.label: Questions on wrongful arrest review
sections.summary: Questions ask whether Police will review procedures after a High Court wrongful arrest finding, including cases of suspected mental disorder.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs in view of the recent finding of wrongful arrest by the High Court, whether the Police will consider reviewing its operating procedures to minimise such occurrences in the future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs in light of the recent court finding that an individual has been wrongly arrested by a Singapore Police Force (SPF) officer (a) whether a review of SPF’s procedures in relation to a person suspected to have a mental disorder has commenced; and (b) whether the incident and the results of any such review will be publicly addressed to maintain confidence in the SPF’s ability to deal with cases of suspected mental disorder.

sections.label: Concern over MHCTA detention impact
sections.summary: Concern that the Court's findings may affect Police detention powers under the MHCTA, with AGC advising on appealing.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Our concern is that the Court's findings may adversely impact the Police's ability to detain persons under the provisions of the MHCTA, as they stand.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Attorney-General's Chambers (AGC) will be advising on whether we should file an application for permission to appeal, in respect of the judgment.

sections.label: Police disciplinary proceedings average
sections.summary: Over the past three years, an average of 78 Police officers faced disciplinary proceedings annually.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: To give Members a sense, over the past three years, an average of 78 Police officers have been subject to disciplinary proceedings annually.

sections.label: Police and AGC consider appeal
sections.summary: The Police and AGC will examine these points and decide whether to appeal the Court's decision.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Police and AGC will look at these points and decide whether the Court's decision should be appealed.

sections.label: Possible appeal or law changes
sections.summary: Comments may affect Police powers and public safety; a decision will follow on appealing or changing the law.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: These comments might have an impact on how the Police can exercise their powers and may have adverse public safety implications.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We will then decide whether to file an application for permission to appeal or make changes to the law as necessary, to address any gaps that may have arisen between the policy intent and the position in law.

sections.label: Concerns with the judgment
sections.summary: In summary, there are concerns with the judgment.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In summary, there are concerns with the judgment.

sections.label: Patrol officers body-worn cameras
sections.summary: Patrol officers wear body-worn cameras, used for a variety of conducts, some in the discharge of duties and some outside.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: On the first question, yes, the patrol officers wear body-worn cameras (BWCs).

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: On the second question, it is for a variety of conducts – some in the discharge of their duties, some are outside.

sections.label: Police intervention imminent danger
sections.summary: The Police can only intervene if there is a threat of imminent danger, violence or assault or something along those lines.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In such a case, the Police can only intervene if there is a threat of imminent danger or violence or assault or something along those lines.
